jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. Stack: TypeScript/Next.js, tRPC, Prisma/MySQL/PlanetScale, Inngest, AWS. I read every HN application myself. Email chris.zehner@fazeshift.com with HN in the subject, your LinkedIn/GitHub/résumé, and a few sentences about something interesting you’ve built or improved recently.

jobs.text: We're building the VMware for GPUs. Most GPUs in the cloud sit idle a lot of the time because they're bolted to one machine over PCIe. We decouple them. Our virtualization layer is a userspace shim, loaded through LD_PRELOAD, that intercepts CUDA calls and ships them over the network to a host with a physical GPU somewhere else in the data center. Workloads run unchanged. When a process goes idle, the GPU detaches and gets reassigned, and reattaches in tens of milliseconds when it's needed again. Think Ceph for GPUs: the GPU becomes a network resource a cluster-wide scheduler can pool and pack. The hard part is making that fast. We're within ~10% of native on most AI workloads, and it lets us serve ~1.8x more users on the same fleet. We run it in production as our own GPU cloud and sell it to enterprises with underutilized fleets. Team is from Citadel Securities, Aquatic, Old Mission, AWS, and Bain. quantaArticles.title: Sea Monkeys Show Scientists How To Rewrite a Rule of Turbulence
quantaArticles.description: Scientists assumed that energy flows in only one direction in a turbulent system. What they didn’t know, until they looked closely at brine shrimp, was that a simple factor can reverse the flow.
quantaArticles.author: Stephen Ornes

quantaArticles.title: What Does the Fourth Dimension Actually Look Like?

quantaArticles.title: Gravity Seems Holographic. What Does That Mean for Reality?
quantaArticles.description: The biggest breakthrough in modern theoretical physics is the discovery that gravity can collapse the dimensions of space. Physicists don’t yet understand the implications.

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Building GenAI Platform at DoorDash
infoqArticles.description: Swaroop Chitlur and Sidd Kodwani share DoorDash’s journey building an internal GenAI platform. They discuss core architectural bets, transitioning from vendor-first setups to open-weights models, navigating LLM and agent gateways, and balancing accuracy, latency, and cost for over 5,000 internal users. By Siddharth Kodwani, Swaroop Chitlur
infoqArticles.author: Siddharth Kodwani, Swaroop Chitlur

infoqArticles.title: Istio 1.31 Adds Agentgateway Waypoints and Moves Release Artifacts off Google Cloud
infoqArticles.description: Istio 1.31 adds agentgateway waypoints in ambient mode, with a canary configuration fix included in 1.31.1. It also ends the publication of images and Helm charts to Google Cloud, requiring repository migration ahead of the 13 October outage test and signing-key updates for teams verifying images. By Mark Silvester
infoqArticles.author: Mark Silvester

infoqArticles.title: AI Agents Are Disrupting Open Source Security Disclosure
infoqArticles.description: A recent article by Anil Madhavapeddy argues that AI agents can turn publicly available clues about software vulnerabilities into working exploits, reducing the effectiveness of traditional disclosure embargoes in open source projects. The author highlights the need for faster patching and release processes as the time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation shrinks. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Uber Eats Rebuilds Search Pipeline to Cut End-to-End Latency by 50%
infoqArticles.description: Uber has rebuilt major parts of the Uber Eats search pipeline, reporting a 50% reduction in end-to-end latency. Changes include Above-the-Fold measurement, reduced retrieval work, parallel hydration, advertising data redesign, infrastructure optimizations, and an agentic coding workflow. Uber is also exploring microbatching, product-based retrieval, and HTTP multipart streaming. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 Tightens Security and Addresses a Difficult Upgrade Path
infoqArticles.description: Envoy Gateway has released v1.9.1, a maintenance release that focuses heavily on security, upgrade reliability, and operational correctness following the broader v1.9 release. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Managing Asynchronous APIs at Scale
infoqArticles.description: Ian Cooper discusses managing asynchronous APIs in event-driven architectures at scale. He explains the "ABCs" of messaging (Address, Binding, Contract) and shares how to tackle discovery, governance, and provisioning using AsyncAPI, CloudEvents, schema registries, and automated CI/CD infrastructure pipelines based on real-world engineering practices at Just Eat Takeaway. By Ian Cooper
infoqArticles.author: Ian Cooper

infoqArticles.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Recap for Developers
infoqArticles.description: OpenAI announced a series of product and developer updates at DevDay 2026, including GPT-6.1 Sol, computer use for the Agents API, cloud-based Codex environments, a Decisions API, and new plugin capabilities for ChatGPT. By Daniel Dominguez
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Dominguez

infoqArticles.title: Engineering Production Systems for an Agentic Era: QCon San Francisco 2026
infoqArticles.description: QCon San Francisco 2026 will bring together practitioners from Airbnb, OpenAI, Netflix, Honeycomb, and other engineering organizations to share how they are building, operating, and evolving production systems as AI agents take on a larger role. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: Article: From Reusable to Regeneratable: Rethinking the Shared UI Component Library
infoqArticles.description: Regeneration has changed reuse economics. A model pointed at a solid design system can produce most standard UI on demand, so paying to keep a canonical component package alive is much harder to justify than it used to be. Keep the design system, tokens, guidelines and tests central. They are what actually buy you consistency. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Packaging AI Agent Permissions as OCI Images
infoqArticles.description: Docker has announced that it is bringing the Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF, aiming to make what an AI agent may access as portable as the agent itself. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
infoqArticles.description: DigitalOcean recently launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview, offering a managed cloud infrastructure layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access, and serverless AI inference. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Qualcomm Unveils Linux Preview on Snapdragon X2 to Accelerate Upstream ARM Laptops
infoqArticles.description: Qualcomm has released an early dev preview of Linux for its upcoming Snapdragon X2 Series laptop processors. The initiative focuses on integrating with the mainline Linux kernel ahead of commercial release to reduce software issues historically faced by ARM laptops. The preview includes a functional Debian 13 environment and aims to standardize system initialization and hardware task management. B
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Beyond Observability: Evolving Production Operations in the Age of AI
infoqArticles.description: The panelists discuss how production operations are evolving with AI, turning operational data into actionable insights for incident response. They explain how automation and new architectural practices help engineering teams build more understandable systems, while exploring how AI reshapes software delivery and changes the historically deterministic nature of production applications. By Michael
infoqArticles.author: Michael Hausenblas, Sujana Sooreddy, Noam Levi, Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: How to Develop Software Engineering Skills in the Age of AI
infoqArticles.description: Software engineering skill development requires slowing down. Generative AI has changed the landscape of skill development for software engineering. Tools and AI can accelerate outcomes, but they may not support skill development. Engineers must understand how systems work to learn things. Senior developers can coach juniors by using learning techniques. By Ben Linders
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Keeping the Mainline Green Across Diverse Language Monorepos
infoqArticles.description: Dhruva Juloori discusses how Uber maintains green mainlines across massive monorepos handling 65,000+ monthly changes. He explains how SubmitQueue uses binary speculation trees, conflict analysis, and machine learning models to predict build success and execution times. Dhruva shares how bypassing large diffs slashed CI resource usage by 53% while accelerating PR landing times by 37%. By Dhruva Ju
infoqArticles.author: Dhruva Juloori
